what_the_frozen_contract_actually_says.source: internal/api/contracts/domain.schema.json, read by walking every enum containing INCONCLUSIVE or ABSTAIN

what_remains_true: The five-class taxonomy the card names DOES exist and is frozen - at the evaluation-case level, which is adapters/evaluation/** and inside this card's write_scope. So action 3 is a wiring and evidence job, not an invention of new vocabulary.

REJECT and WATCH exist at Goal.outcome, not at Experiment.outcome. Asking the experiment to carry them would be a category error; the honest reading of the card's '支持REJECT/WATCH/INCONCLUSIVE' is the disposition the experiment feeds into, which is where those values already live.

INVALID is in NO enum anywhere in the frozen contract. The card names it and the contract does not carry it. That is a real finding and it is now the interesting one: either the card's sixth class maps onto an existing value (MetricResult.NOT_RUN or EvaluationCaseResult.MISSING) or the contract needs its owner to change it, which this card's limits forbid.
one_real_defect_found_while_checking: metricStatus (internal/domain/experiments.go:247-283) switches on the frozen operator set and has no default branch, so a metric carrying an unrecognised operator falls through with pass=false and is reported as FAIL. A gate that could not be evaluated is being recorded as a measured shortfall, which is the one thing the card's own counter-example forbids: an unrunnable measurement must not imply an outcome. The fix stays inside the frozen enum - an operator the contract does not define can only be INCONCLUSIVE or NOT_RUN, never FAIL.
consequence_for_the_card: The build is smaller and better-aimed than the inventory implied: produce and retain the five evaluation-case verdicts through the experiment path, fix the missing switch default, decide and document how INVALID is represented without editing a frozen contract, and cover the 12 frozen smoke cases, which genuinely are not named by any program.
how_i_want_to_be_read: This correction makes the card's scope narrower than I first told myself, not larger, which is the direction an executor is least tempted to catch. The same grep, run one file wider, would have produced it correctly the first time.
